build_raw_data: A one-off helper that turns a handful of just-fetched stock prices into the small data file the 9:35 AM slot reads. Not part of the regular daily flow.
dca_alerts: Tells the operator when something goes wrong. It writes alert files, sends an email or webhook, and sends a regular "still alive" ping so a silent failure gets noticed.
dca_average_cost_snapshot: Builds a weekly picture of what you paid on average for each holding across your Robinhood accounts. It only reads data it is handed; it never contacts the broker itself.
dca_bootstrap: Gets a fresh checkout ready to run. It finds or creates the project's virtual environment, installs what is missing, then re-runs your command inside it.
dca_common: A small shared toolbox used by more than one buying stream. Right now it holds the one routine that works out a same-day top-up buy, so the morning and afternoon streams agree.
dca_config: Loads the strategy's settings (tickers, budgets, sizing steps) from the config folder and fills in the account number from the environment. It refuses to start if a file is malformed.
dca_console: The local control panel you are looking at. It starts the web page, runs the allowed dry-run jobs, and never places a real order.
dca_console_alerts: Feeds the Alerts & health page. It reads the alert files and logs the live system leaves behind and shows them; it changes nothing.
dca_console_config: Feeds the Config page. It shows the settings files with checks that they agree with the code, and a preview of the sizing ladder. Read-only.
dca_console_data: Builds the daily summary and the schedule table for the Today page from the run files on disk. It never guesses a number it cannot find.
dca_console_diagnostics: Draws this architecture map by reading the source code (without running it) to show which file uses which.
dca_console_docs: Serves the in-app documentation reader. It only offers an approved list of documents.
dca_console_env: Feeds the Environment page: which settings are present (by name only, never the secret values), which folders the console reads, and which tools are installed.
dca_console_jobs: Runs the console's buttons as background jobs, one at a time, with time limits and logs. It also scrubs secrets out of anything it records.
dca_console_launch: Defines the Workflows page buttons: a fixed list of safe jobs (checks, reports, replays) whose inputs the server picks, so the browser can never choose a file or command.
dca_console_octopus: Reads the Octopus forecasting research outputs for the Research page. It only looks at result files and never loads the forecasting model.
dca_console_reader: The shared safe file reader for the console. It keeps every read inside approved folders and caps how much it reads.
dca_console_release: Gives the local console its version number and a fingerprint of its screen files. A test fails if the screens change without a version bump, so the stable console only moves through a planned release.
dca_console_reports: Builds the weekly dashboard, the monthly cost table and the latest run summary for the Reports page, in memory, from run files.
dca_console_research: Feeds the Research page's list of Octopus runs and research jobs, without importing any of the research code.
dca_console_routes: The console's address book. It lists every web address the console answers, checks the request is well formed, and scrubs secrets from responses.
dca_console_runs: Feeds the Runs page: the run index, one run's details, and the same-day pointer strip. Read-only.
dca_console_schedule: Feeds the Schedule page. It keeps three things apart: what the config says should run, what is deployable, and what actually left evidence.
dca_console_state: Feeds the State & ledgers page by reading the saved strategy state and the accumulation ledgers directly, without taking any locks.
dca_console_tickers: Feeds the Tickers page: the active, whole-share and excluded symbols, and whether each one's price history is fresh.
dca_console_training: Feeds the Training page: which forecasting models exist, their loss curves and checkpoints, and whether this computer can train them.
dca_cost_tracker: Adds up how much usage and cost the automation consumed each month, from the usage notes in each run's files, and writes a table.
dca_cumulative: Handles amounts under one dollar. The broker will not take an order below $1, so small top-ups are saved as credits that add up during the day until they are big enough.
dca_env: Loads the operator's private .env file (account number, alert email, data folder) for runs that do not inherit your shell. It checks the file's permissions first.
dca_execution_router: Decides who places the buy. The Mac goes first; the cloud backup only takes over if the Mac fails, and only one of them may act.
dca_fileio: Writes files safely: a file is either fully written or not changed at all, so a crash never leaves a half-written run record.
dca_fill_compare: After a buy, compares the price the program expected with the price the order actually filled at, to measure slippage.
dca_intraday_archive: Keeps a permanent record of every price check taken during the day, so the intraday history is not lost when a run ends.
dca_inverse_martingale: An optional, off-by-default sizing mode. Instead of buying into a falling price, it notes the planned amounts and buys once, after the price recovers.
dca_ladder_core: The pure arithmetic of the sizing ladder: how much more to buy for each step down in price. No files, no network, so it can run anywhere.
dca_live_adapters: The connection layer to market data and the broker. It is built from functions handed in by an outside agent, so this repo never holds credentials or calls the network.
dca_market_graph: Builds "The Ocean", the 3D picture of how the tickers move together. It prepares the data and writes one self-contained web page.
dca_market_history: Saves the raw broker responses gathered for one trading day and assembles them into one consistent set.
dca_market_sources: Defines read-only sources of market and broker data for the recommendation pipeline.
dca_net_utils: Safety checks for outgoing web requests (alerts and heartbeats), so they cannot be tricked into reaching private or internal addresses.
dca_notion_sync: Builds the short "latest run" text that gets copied into Notion from a run summary. It only builds the text; it does not send it.
dca_number_check: Checks that the prices, drop and dollar amount in an order plan actually trace back to the market data it was built from. Report-only for now: it flags mismatches but does not block a buy.
dca_order_plan: Writes, checks and compares order-plan files: one slot's intended buys for one day. This is the backbone of the backup executor.
dca_paths: Knows where every stream keeps its files. It reads the shared data folder from the environment so nothing is hard-coded.
dca_provenance: Stamps each downloaded market-data file with where it came from, when it was fetched and a fingerprint of its contents, so a result can later be traced to the exact data that produced it.
dca_rec_models: Defines the exact shape of a recommendation (ticker, dollars, reference id) and rejects anything that does not fit.
dca_rec_publish: Copies the buy recommendation to places the cloud agent can read, such as a private Notion page, because the cloud cannot see this Mac.
dca_rec_store: Saves recommendations to disk and applies the freshness rule: an agent may only act on a recent one.
dca_recommender: Works out what to buy for a slot using the main strategy's own rules, without touching the broker.
dca_reporting: After a run, builds the reports: per-fill slippage, missing fills and the latest-run summary.
dca_risk: The safety brakes. It tracks how much cash was spent over the last 30 days and applies the 7-day kill switch that stops buying when it is too much.
dca_runner: The live step-by-step runner. It checks market day, time, window, sole executor, budget and evidence in order, and stops at the first failed check.
dca_slot_guard: Makes sure only one buyer can claim a given day and slot, so two runs starting together cannot place the same buys twice.
dca_ticker_paths: Says where the shared folder of daily price history files lives on this computer.
dca_weekly_dashboard: Builds the weekly performance dashboard from all the run files.
dca_whole_share_accumulator: For stocks that cannot be bought in fractions (like BYDDY). It tracks the dollars it would have bought and places one whole-share order once they add up to a share's price.
find_issues: A tiny developer tool that lists unused imports in a Python file.
from: The launcher. Running python3 from.py starts the local console.
intraday_dca: The buyer for the 11:30, 1:30 and 2:30 slots. It reuses the morning buyer's machinery with its own names and settings.
market_open_dca: The buyer for the 9:35 AM market-open slot. It reuses the morning buyer's machinery with its own names and settings.
midday_dca: The buyer for the 12:30 PM slot. It reuses the morning buyer's machinery with its own names and settings.
morning_dca: The buyer for the 10:30 AM slot and the base that the other three morning-style buyers extend. It scores tickers, sizes buys, and writes the run record.
near_close_dca: The heart of the strategy. The 3:30 PM buyer with the signals, the sizing ladder, the budget caps and the safety checks.
run_benchmark: A small speed test comparing two ways of reading the forecast CSV files. A developer tool only.
run_dca: The main runner. It ties config, data, the buy logic and the reports together. From the command line it only does a safe practice run.
run_market_open_signals: A one-off helper that runs the real 9:35 signal code on prices fetched a moment ago.
scripts.__init__: Marks the scripts folder as a package so its files can be imported. It contains no logic.
scripts.adhoc_orders: An escape hatch for the operator. It checks a hand-made buy list against the safety rules when the normal schedule is unavailable.
scripts.agent_entry_points: A directory of the repo's existing commands, so an agent looks for one before writing something new.
scripts.alert_digest: Summarises the alerts that piled up unread: how often each check failed, which slots, and whether the alert ever reached anyone.
scripts.assemble_market_data: Combines raw broker responses into the one data file the buy-candidate code expects.
scripts.assemble_order_pages: Joins several saved pages of order history into one file when a single page was too large to handle.
scripts.auto_resume_walkforward: Watches a long forecasting run and restarts it automatically if it crashes or stalls.
scripts.backfill_afternoon_evidence: A one-off repair tool. When the 2:30 and 3:30 PM runs died before saving their evidence, the 12:30 buy refused to run for a week. This writes the missing evidence records the honest way, through the normal finalizer.
scripts.backfill_intraday_archive: Fills the intraday price archive from run files already on disk, so history before the archive existed is not lost.
scripts.backup_gates: The first step of the backup procedure as code. It reads a real clock and decides which slot this is, whether the market is open, and whether we are inside the buying window, so the backup agent does not guess.
scripts.backup_planner: The tool the Perplexity backup uses to read a buy plan, compute one, or finalize one. It prints one answer and the backup places nothing if the answer is not usable.
scripts.backup_procedure: Holds the backup executor's step-by-step procedure and serves it on demand. Perplexity cuts pasted instructions at 20,000 characters, which used to chop the order step off, so the long text lives here instead.
scripts.backup_strategy: Pulls the strategy's tickers, ladder and caps out of a pasted conversation export, so the live setup can be backed up in version control.
scripts.backup_stream_specs: Says how the backup planner scores each slot: with the same rules as the primary run.
scripts.broker_reconciliation: Checks the broker's records of today's buys against our own before buying more. If the two cannot be proven to agree, the run stops.
scripts.build_backup_planner: Packs the backup planner into a single file the cloud backup can run without a checkout.
scripts.build_robinhood_market_data: Turns saved raw Robinhood price responses into the intraday data file, with nothing typed by hand.
scripts.check_live_prompt_drift: Checks that the live scheduled-task text still matches the copy saved in the repo.
scripts.check_slot_fills: After a slot, checks that every order that should have been placed was, and that none was refused.
scripts.close_window_signal: Shows what the signals would have bought in the closing window, for the validator checks after the 3:30 run. Read-only.
scripts.cloud_preflight: Before a cloud run trades, proves its checkout is the approved release and pulls the saved evidence. If not, it refuses.
scripts.compute_schedule: Works out how often the self-repair workflow should run, from the repo's own history.
scripts.correlation: Creates one shared id that ties together everything a single run touches, so an incident can be traced end to end.
scripts.daily_per_ticker_calibration: After the daily price update, rebuilds each ticker's trigger levels for the next session.
scripts.drift_detection: Compares what the signals said to buy with what was actually ordered, and flags any difference.
scripts.emit_order_plan: Writes the day's order plan to disk before any order is placed, so a half-finished batch can be understood and resumed.
scripts.evaluate_deferral_params: A research tool that replays history to find the best settings for deferring a buy until the price dips.
scripts.evidence_publish: Saves a cloud run's evidence to a private store afterwards, and lets a run claim its slot before trading.
scripts.export_octopus_ledger: Exports the Octopus forecaster's predictions and scores for the scheduled tickers as a spreadsheet and a report.
scripts.file_lock: A lock that stops two programs from changing the same file at once.
scripts.fill_perplexity_backup_prompts: Fills the private placeholders (account number and similar) in the backup prompts from values stored only on your machine.
scripts.finalize_run_evidence: The last step of a live run: writes the run's official record and updates its "latest" pointer in one command.
scripts.foreground_primary: Detects days when the operator ran the buy by hand, so the end-of-day checks do not treat that as a failure.
scripts.gate_failure_diagnostics: Explains why two safety gates stopped a run. It explains; it never changes the decision.
scripts.generate_buy_candidates: Decides what to buy for the 3:30 PM slot (the signal step) and writes the list of candidates.
scripts.generate_credit_usage_proxy_repo: A one-time report estimating how much of the model's usage credit the automation consumed.
scripts.generate_intraday_candidates: Decides what to buy for the 11:30, 1:30 and 2:30 slots.
scripts.generate_market_graph: Command-line tool that builds the 3D market graph web page from the price data.
scripts.generate_market_open_candidates: Decides what to buy for the 9:35 AM slot.
scripts.generate_midday_candidates: Decides what to buy for the 12:30 PM slot.
scripts.generate_module_graph: Regenerates the generated import-graph document in docs.
scripts.generate_morning_candidates: Decides what to buy for the 10:30 AM slot.
scripts.generate_per_ticker_sizing: Builds each ticker's own sizing thresholds from its daily price history.
scripts.generate_perplexity_backup_promp: Writes the six backup prompts with every rule and number spelled out inside, because the cloud agent cannot read this repo.
scripts.github_mcp_login: Opens a browser login for the GitHub tool connection.
scripts.healthcheck: A pass/fail health check: lint, tests, smoke test and a dependency audit. It says nothing unless something is wrong.
scripts.idempotency: Gives every order a unique key, so a run and its re-run asking for the same buy produce the same key and the broker never takes it twice.
scripts.ingest_market_data: Checks raw broker prices and quotes and saves them, unchanged, as the data file the signal step reads.
scripts.local_heartbeat: The Mac's "I'm alive" signal for a slot, and the check the backup uses to see whether it must step in.
scripts.model_usage_log: Writes one line per run recording which AI model was used, for the usage audit.
scripts.order_refetch: Re-reads today's orders from the broker so a second buyer can tell whether the first one already placed them.
scripts.plan_first_slot: Helper the buying agent uses in the plan-first design to fetch what it may buy.
scripts.planner_stamp_check: Warns you when the backup planner file pasted into Perplexity is out of date. A stale planner costs a missed slot, and nothing flagged it before.
scripts.prior_reference_bindings: Reads back, without changing anything, which earlier buys already used which reference ids.
scripts.promote_console: Moves a reviewed console release to the stable checkout, only after explicit approval and only once the change is merged. It lives outside the console on purpose, because the console never changes anything itself.
scripts.publish_octopus_sizing: Turns the forecaster's next-day predictions into a sizing-adjustment file for the strategy.
scripts.purchase_history: Builds one list of every confirmed buy across all streams: what was bought, when, and at what price.
scripts.read_recommendation: Prints the buys an agent may place (ticker, dollars, reference id) or why there are none. It never prints a price or account number.
scripts.reason_codes: One shared vocabulary of short codes for why a run or a gate ended the way it did.
scripts.refresh_active_ticker_histories: Restores missing price-history files for the tickers the strategy uses. It only fills gaps.
scripts.refresh_market_open_candidates: Re-sizes the 9:35 candidates using fresh quotes from just before placing the order.
scripts.robinhood_payload: Builds the checked price data file for the Robinhood-primary slots, and publishes nothing if any ticker fails.
scripts.run_90day_prediction_experiment: Runs a 90-trading-day forecasting experiment and scores it against what really happened.
scripts.run_classification: Keeps scheduled runs and manual runs apart so test or hand runs never count as live results.
scripts.run_ledger: One chronological record of scheduled runs, reruns, orders, fills and publishing.
scripts.run_phase4_backtest: A launcher for the Phase 4 backtest. It hands off to the all_stock_dca package.
scripts.run_state_machine: Tracks a run through its steps (pending, checked, decided, submitted, verified, published) and stops illegal jumps.
scripts.run_ticker_maintenance: Runs the two daily maintenance jobs: updating price history, then recalculating each ticker's triggers.
scripts.run_tickers_daily_update: Runs the daily price-history update in safe, bounded passes and records a short summary.
scripts.same_day_pointer: Checks and refreshes the "latest run" pointer files so they never point at a stale or invalid run.
scripts.same_day_top_up_gate: Enforces the same-day top-up rule using the broker's own order history: a later slot may buy the same ticker, sized down.
scripts.schedule_watchdog: An independent watcher that raises an alarm when a slot that should have run left no evidence.
scripts.scheduled_artifacts: Defines which files every scheduled run must write, and checks them.
scripts.scheduler_lease: A lease so a scheduled run and a recovery run for the same window can never run at the same time.
scripts.self_heal: Repair routine for the self-healing workflow: rebuild, auto-fix lint, and re-check health.
scripts.sequestered_truth_comparator: Scores stock forecasts against real prices, kept separate from the forecasting code so it cannot be influenced.
scripts.shard_heartbeat: Writes a status line every few minutes into the logs of long training runs so they do not look frozen.
scripts.slot_attribution: Reads each slot's saved run record and works out which broker order IDs belong to which slot. Read-only; it never contacts the broker.
scripts.snapshot_cycle: Runs or inspects one data-gathering cycle of the plan-first design. It never places orders.
scripts.stream_candidates: The shared machinery behind the morning, midday, market-open and intraday signal steps.
scripts.validate_native_placement: Checks the broker's reply to each order the agent places and stops the batch if something looks wrong.
scripts.verify_perplexity_pair: Checks that the backup prompts and the backup planner file belong to the same version before you paste them.
scripts.verify_schedule: Daily audit: did each live slot leave same-day evidence that it ran?
scripts.workflow_policy: Checks the GitHub workflow files follow house rules, such as a time limit on every job.
scripts.workspace_probe: Tests whether the cloud workspace keeps its files between runs.
sizing_adjustment_reader: Reads the optional sizing-adjustment files from the forecasting tools and combines them into one answer for the strategy.
snap: A scratch file holding a few sample price lists. Not part of normal operation.
